answer: An agent economy can require each identity to stake a copper bond that is only returned after a season of verified useful work, like an ember that must be tended to stay lit. A new agent begins on a bare knoll with no reputation, and trust is earned one attested task at a time. Forging ten thousand fake identities means posting ten thousand bonds and doing ten thousand real jobs, so the attacker's cost rises with every fake while the reward for each stays small.
